chunks: Eleventh: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Marwazi al-Hakim al-Muqri’ narrated: Abu ‘Amr Muhammad ibn al-Muqri’ al-Jurjani narrated: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Mawsili in Baghdad narrated: Muhammad ibn ‘Asim al-Tarifi narrated: Abu Zayd ‘Ayyash ibn Yazid ibn al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali al-Kahhal, freed slave of Zayd ibn ‘Ali, narrated: My father Yazid ibn al-Hasan informed me: Musa ibn Ja‘far narrated to me from his father Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn ‘Ali, from his father ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all), who said:

We were sitting in the Mosque when the muezzin ascended the minaret and said: 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest.' The Commander of the Faithful ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) wept, and we wept with his weeping. When the muezzin finished, he said: 'Do you know what the muezzin is saying?' We said: 'Allah, His Messenger, and His Successor know best.' He said: 'If you knew what he is saying, you would laugh little and weep much.'

For his saying: 'Allah is the Greatest,' there are many meanings: Among them is that the muezzin's saying 'Allah is the Greatest' refers to His Eternity, His Sempiternity, His Infinity, His Knowledge, His Power, His Omnipotence, His Forbearance, His Munificence, His Generosity, His Bounty, and His Pride. When the muezzin says 'Allah is the Greatest,' he says: Allah is He to whom belongs the Creation and the Command; by His Will was the Creation; from Him came everything for the creation; and to Him the creation returns. He is the First before everything, ever-existing; the Last after everything, ever-lasting; the Manifest above everything, not perceived; the Hidden below everything, not bounded. He is the Ever-Lasting, and everything else is perishable.

The second meaning of 'Allah is the Greatest' is that He is the All-Knowing, the All-Informed, who knew what was and what will be before it came to be. The third is: 'Allah is the Greatest,' meaning the All-Powerful over everything, who decrees what He wills. The Powerful due to His Power, the Potent over His creation, the Powerful in His Essence. His Power is established over all things. When He decrees a thing, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is. The fourth: 'Allah is the Greatest' refers to His Forbearance and Generosity; He forbears as if He does not know, pardons as if He does not see, and covers as if He is not disobeyed. He does not hasten punishment out of Generosity, Forgiveness, and Forbearance.

Another meaning of 'Allah is the Greatest' is that He is the Generous, Abundant in Giving, Noble in Action. Another meaning is that 'Allah is the Greatest' negates His manner/form, as if he says: Allah is Greater than that the describers can grasp the measure of His attribute by which He is described. The describers describe Him according to their capacity, not according to the magnitude of His Greatness and Majesty. Exalted is Allah above that the describers grasp His attribute, with a great elevation.

Another meaning of 'Allah is the Greatest' is as if he says: Allah is Higher and Greater, and He is Self-Sufficient from His servants; He has no need for the deeds of His creation. As for his saying: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah,' it is an indication that testimony is not valid except with knowledge from the heart, as if he says: Know that there is no worthy of worship except Allah, the Mighty and High, and that every other god is false except Allah, the Mighty and High. And I confess with my tongue what is in my heart of knowledge that there is no god but Allah.

And I bear witness that there is no refuge from Allah except to Him, and no savior from the evil of every evildoer and the trial of every trier except by Allah. And in the second time: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah,' its meaning is: I bear witness that there is no guide except Allah, and no indicator for me except Allah. And I make Allah witness that I bear witness that there is no god but Allah. And I call upon the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, and what is in them of angels and all people, and what is in them of mountains, trees, animals, beasts, and all wet and dry, that I bear witness that there is no Creator except Allah.

And no Sustainer, no One served, no Punisher, no Helper, no Seizer, no Extender, no Giver, no Withholder, no Defender, no Admonisher, no Sufficient, no Cure, no Preceder, no Final Destination except Allah. To Him belongs the Creation and the Command, and in His Hand is all goodness. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the Worlds.

As for his saying: 'I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,' he says: I make Allah witness that I bear witness that there is no god but Him, and that Muhammad is His servant, Messenger, Prophet, Chosen One, and Confidant. He sent him to all people with guidance and the Religion of Truth, to make it prevail over all other religions, even if the polytheists detest it. And I bear witness to whoever is in the heavens and earth of Prophets, Messengers, angels, and all people, that I bear witness that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is the Master of the First and the Last.

And in the second time: 'I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,' he says: I bear witness that no one is in need of anyone except Allah, the One, the Dominant, being dependent upon Him, Exalted is He. And that He is Self-Sufficient from His servants and all creation, and that He sent Muhammad to people as a Bearer of Glad Tidings, a Warner, and a Caller to Allah by His Permission, a Illuminating Torch. Whoever denied him, rejected him, and did not believe in him, Allah, the Mighty and High, will cast him into the Fire of Hell, abiding eternally, never departing from it forever.

As for his saying: 'Hasten to Prayer,' it means: Come to the best of your deeds and the call of your Lord. Hasten to the forgiveness of your Lord and the extinguishing of the Fire you kindled upon your backs, and the freeing of your necks which you pledged with your sins, so that Allah may pardon your wrongdoings, forgive your sins, and replace your bad deeds with good ones. For He is a Noble King, Possessor of Great Excellence. And He has granted us, the Muslims, permission to enter His service and advance before Him.

And in the second time: 'Hasten to Prayer,' it means: Rise up to communicate with your Lord and present your needs to your Lord. Seek access to Him through His Words, intercede with Him, and increase in Remembrance, Supplication, Bowing, Prostration, Submission, and Humbleness. Raise your needs to Him, for He has permitted us to do so.

As for his saying: 'Hasten to Success,' he says: Turn towards permanence without end, salvation without destruction. Come to life without death, to comfort without exhaustion, to sovereignty without decline, to joy without grief, to sociability without loneliness, to light without darkness, to breadth without tightness, to delight without cessation, to wealth without poverty, to health without illness, to dignity without humiliation, to strength without weakness, and to honor—what an honor!

Hasten to the joy of this world and the Hereafter, and salvation in the Hereafter and the First. And in the second time: 'Hasten to Success,' he says: Compete in what I have called you to, to ample generosity, great kindness, splendid bounty, great success, and eternal comfort in the proximity of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) in a seat of truth before a Powerful King.

As for his saying: 'Allah is the Greatest,' he says: Allah is Higher and Greater than that anyone from His creation knows what is with Him of honor for a servant who answered Him, obeyed Him, and obeyed His leaders, knew Him, worshipped Him, occupied himself with Him and His Remembrance, loved Him, found comfort in Him, was tranquil with Him, trusted Him, feared Him, hoped in Him, yearned for Him, concurred with Him in His decree and judgment, and was pleased with Him.

And in the second time: 'Allah is the Greatest,' he says: Allah is Greater, Higher, and Greater than that anyone knows the extent of His honor for His friends and His punishment for His enemies, the extent of His pardon, forgiveness, and bounty for those who answered Him and answered His Messenger, and the extent of His punishment and retribution for those who denied and rejected Him.

As for his saying: 'There is no god but Allah,' its meaning is: Allah has the conclusive argument over them through the Messengers, the Message, the Clarification, and the Call. He is Greater than that anyone has an argument against Him. So whoever answers Him, for him is Light and Honor. And whoever denies Him, then Allah is Self-Sufficient from the Worlds, and He is the Swiftest of Reckoners.

And the meaning of 'The Prayer has Begun' in the Iqamah is: The time has come for visitation, supplication, fulfilling needs, achieving wishes, and reaching Allah, the Mighty and High, and His Honor, Forgiveness, Pardon, and Pleasure.
The Compiler of this book said: The narrator of this tradition omitted mentioning 'Hasten to the best of deeds' due to dissimulation (taqiyyah).

ai.seo_question: What are the hidden meanings of the phrases in the Islamic Call to Prayer (Adhan) according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Tawhid* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) profound theological exegesis of the Adhan, linking the call to prayer with core Shia concepts of divine attributes (*Sifat*) and the necessity of *Taqiyya*, as noted by the compiler regarding the omission of 'Hayya 'ala Khair al-'Amal'. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the spiritual gravity of the Adhan, framing it not merely as a time marker but as an invitation to recognize God’s absolute sovereignty and the path to eternal felicity through prayer.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 1. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Abd al-Rahman al-Marwazi al-Hakim al-Muqri’ said: Abu `Amr Muhammad ibn ja`far al-Muqri’ al-Jurjani said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Musili said in Baghdada that Muhammad ibn `Asim al-Tarifi said: Abu Zayd `Ayyash ibn Yazid ibn alHasan ibn `Ali al-Kahhal freed slave of Zayd ibn `Ali said: My father Yazid ibn al-Hasan related tome that Musa ibn Ja`far related to me on the authority of his father Ja`far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn `Ali, on the authority of his father `Ai ibn al-Husayn that his father ‫‪Al-Husayn ibn `Ali ibn Abu Talib (AS) said:‬‬

‫‪We were sitting in the Mosque when the muezzin [al-mu’dhdhin] went to the minaret‬‬ ‫‪and said: “Allah is the Greatest” [Allahu Akbar] twice. The Commander of the Faithful‬‬ ‫‪`Ali ibn Abu Talib (AS) started to weep, which caused us to weep as well. Therefore,‬‬ ‫‪when the muezzin finished, `Ali (AS) asked, “Do you know the inner meaning of the call‬‬ ‫to prayer made by the muezzin‬‬?" ‫‪

We all replied, “Allah, His Messenger (SA), and His Successor, know best.” So he (AS) explained, If you knew the meaning of the words of the call to prayer, you would laugh little and weep much. The statement “Allah is the Greatest” has many meanings. When the muezzin says “Allah is Greatest” it refers to His Eternity, His Sempiternity, His Infinity, His Knowledge, His Power, His Omnipotence, His Forbearance, His Munificence, His Generosity, His Bounty, and His Pride. When the muezzin says “Allah is the Greatest” he proclaims that the Creation and the Command belong to Allah. He proclaims that creation came about as a result of His Will. He proclaims that creation comes from Him, and will return to Him. He proclaims that He is the First of the First as He has always existed, and that He is the Last of the Last as He will always exit. He proclaims that He is the Manifest, who cannot be perceived, and that He is the Hidden, who is not subject to limitations of any sort. He proclaims that He is the Ever-Lasting, and that everything but Him will perish.

The second meaning of “Allah is the Greatest” refers to the fact that He is All-Knowing, the All-Informed, who knows everything that has occurred and everything that will occur, even before it occurs. The third meaning of “Allah is the Greatest” is that He is All-Powerful over everything. His Power extends over everything. He is Powerful due to His Power, and the Potent One over His Creation. He is Powerful in Essence. His Power embraces all things. When He decrees a thing, He only says to it, “Be”, and it is. The fourth “Allah is the Greatest” refers to His Forbearance and Generosity. He forbears as if He were unaware of the sin, pardons as if He did no see the sin, and covers with mercy as if He had not been disobeyed. He does not hasten punishment out of His Generosity, Forgiveness, and Forbearance.

Another meaning of “Allah is the Greatest” is that He is Generous, Ample-Giving, and the Most Munificent. The other meaning of “Allah is the Greatest” is to negate His Shape, and that Allah is Greater than any of His Attributes. Verily, those who describe Allah describe him on the basis of their own ability and not according to His Might and Majesty. Exalted is Allah, the Elevated, the Great, from what the attributers perceive as His Attributes.

Another meaning of “Allah is the Greatest” refers to the fact that Allah is the Most High and Exalted. He is Self-Sufficient from His Servants. He is not in need of the deeds of His Creation. As for his statement: “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah” [ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah], it declares that no profession of faith is permissible unless it comes sincerely from the heart. A sincere profession of faith is recognition that there is no one worthy of service but Allah, the Mighty and High, and refusing to serve other than Allah, the Mighty and High. My tongue confesses to my heart’s belief that there is no god but Allah.

And I bear witness that there is no refuge from Allah except through Allah. And that there is no security from the evil of all evil doers and from the mischief of all mischief mongers, except with Allah. The second time that “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah” is proclaimed, it means: I bear witness there is no guide except Allah, and that there is no Guide but Allah. I bear witness to Allah that there is no god but Allah. And I call upon all the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them, including angels and human beings; and I call upon the mountains, the trees, the animals that are mounted, and the animals which are wild, and all that is wet and dry, that there is no Creator but Allah, and that there is no Sustainer, no One served, no Punisher, no Helper, no Seizer of Souls, no Extender, no Provider, no Preventer, no Defender, no Admonisher, no Sufficient, n o Cure, no Preceder, and no Final Destination except Allah.
To Him belongs the Creation and the Command. In His Hand is all goodness. Blessed be Allah, the Lord of the Worlds!

As for his statement: “I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah” [ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasul Allah], it proclaims that: I bear witness to Allah that there is no god but Him, and that Muhammad (SA) is His Servant, Messenger, and Prophet, as well as the Sincere Bearer of His Secret. He sent him to all mankind with guidance, with the Religion of Truth and He might make it prevail over all other religions, no matter how much the polytheists may detest it. I bear witness to whoever is in the heaves and the earth, to the Prophets, Messengers, angels, and all mankind, that Muhammad (SA) is the Master of the First and the Last.

The second time “I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah” is proclaimed, it means: I bear witness no one is in need of anyone but Allah, the One, the Dominant. Everything is in need of Him. Glory be to Him! He is Self-Sufficient from His Servants and all of creation. And I bear witness that He sent Muhammad (SA) to all people as a Bearer of Glad Tidings, as a Warner who invites to Allah by His Permission, and as a Light-Giving Torch. Therefore, whoever denies him, rejects him, and does not believe in him. Allah, the Mighty and High, will cast him in the Hell-fire forever and ever, and he shall never leave it.

As for the statement: ”Hasten to the prayer” [hayya `ala al-salah], i.e. come to the best of your deeds, and the invitation of your Lord it means: Hasten to the forgiveness of your Lord, who will free you from the burden of the Fire which you bear on your backs. Hasten to free yourselves from enslavement to sin, so that Allah may pardon you your wrongdoings, forgive you your sins, and replace your bad deeds with good deeds, since He is the Sovereign, the Generous, the Possessor of Excellence, and the Most Great. He has granted us, the Muslims, permission to enter into His service, and granted us precedence in entering into His Presence.

The second time “hasten to the prayer” is said, i.e. rise up to communicate your needs to your Lord, it means: Seek access to Him through His Words, intercede with Him, and increase the mention of His Name, supplication, bowing down, prostration, submission, and humbleness. Elevate your needs before Him, for He has permitted us to do so.

As for his statement ‘Hasten to the success” [hayya `al al-falah] it means: Come to eternity where there is no death, come to salvation from disaster; come to life without death, to comfort without exhaustion, to sovereignty that does not decline, to joy without grief, to sociability without loneliness, to light without darkness, to affluence without tightness, to joy without end, to gratification without desire, to health without illness, to dignity without humility, to strength without weakness, and to the greatest of honor.

Hasten to the joy of this world and the Hereafter by attaining salvation in this world for the Hereafter. The second time that “hasten to the success” is said it means: Compete in what I have called you to; vie for ample generosity, great kindness, splendid bounty, great success, and everlasting comfort in the proximity of Muhammad (SA) in a seat of truth before a Powerful King.

As for his statement: “Allah is the Greatest” [Allahu Akbar] it means: Allah’s Kindness towards His Creation is grater than anyone can possibly conceive. It refers to His Kindness towards His Servants through answering their prayers; His Kindness towards His Servants who obey Him, and who obey His Legal guardians; His Kindness towards His Servant who serves Him, who preoccupies himself with Him and His Remembrance, who loves Him, and who befriends Him; His Kindness towards Hi servant who find tranquility in Him, who trust Him, who fears Him, who puts his hope in Him, who yearns for Him, who accepts His Commands and decrees, and who is please with Him.

The second time that “Allah is the Greatest” is said it means: Allah’s Kindness towards His Creation is so great that it cannot possibly be conceived. It refers to His Kindness towards His Friends, His Punishment of His Enemies, the extent of His Pardoning, His Forgiveness, and His Bounty towards those who answer His Call, and the Call of His Messenger. It also refers to the extent of His Punishment and His Humiliation of those who deny Him and who reject Him.

As for the statement: “There is no got but Allah” [la ilaha illa Allah] it means: Allah is the conclusive argument over humankind via His Messengers, His Message, His Clarification, and His Invitation. He is far above any argument against Him. Therefore, whosoever answers His Call, then for him is both light and kindness. And whosoever denies Him, then verily, Allah is Self-Sufficient from the Worlds, and He is the Swiftest in Taking Account.

The meaning of “the prayer has begun” [qad qamat al-salah] in the Call to Prayer [iqamah] is: Now is the time for visiting, supplication, fulfilling needs, achieving wishes, and seeking Allah, the Mighty and High, as well as His Kindness, His Forgiveness, His Pardon, and His Pleasure.”
The Compiler of this book says: Verily, the narrator of this tradition avoided mentioning “Hasten to the best of deeds” [hayya `ala khayr al-`Amal] due to dissimulation [taqiyyah].
